html:
The Ramkokamekrá are one of the two Canela peoples of the dry savanna of Maranhão, northeastern Brazil, near Barra do Corda. They speak a Timbira language of the Jê family.

Like other Timbira peoples such as the Apanyekrá, the Apinayé and the Krikati, they live in large circular villages with paths running to a central plaza, and hold log races in which teams run carrying heavy sections of palm trunk. Cattle ranchers pressed into their land from the 1700s. The German born ethnologist Curt Nimuendajú described them in the 1930s.
sum: The Ramkokamekrá are one of the two Canela peoples of the dry savanna of Maranhão, northeastern Brazil, near Barra do Corda. They speak a Timbira language of the Jê family.
